production.note: US model years 2021 to 2025. First: PCNA presents the car among 'New equipment for Porsche mid-engine sports cars for the 2021 model year' ('The 718 Cayman GTS 4.0 and 718 Boxster GTS 4.0, which both make 394 hp'); Car and Driver's panel is for a '2021 Porsche 718 Cayman GTS 4.0' (cd-2021-718-cayman-gts-4-0). Last: Kelley Blue Book's 2025 page lists the 'GTS 4.0' trim ('the GTS 4.0 has a 4.0-liter engine. It develops 394 horsepower') and says production of the 718 Cayman 'is set to end' in 'October 2025' (kbb-2025-718-cayman). No opened Porsche page states that 2025 was the last US model year.

body.note: C/D panel: '2-door hatchback' (rear hatch); the guide files such cars as Coupe. The open car is sold under its own name (718 Boxster GTS 4.0).

fuel.note: Inferred from the panel's description ('direct fuel injection' gasoline flat-6).

transmission.note: The six-speed manual is standard ('the standard six-speed manual (309 lb.-ft.)'); the 4.0-liter 718 models 'have been available to order with the optional seven-speed Porsche dual-clutch transmission (PDK) since June in the U.S.' DCT is Porsche PDK.

powerHp.note: Quote: "The 718 Cayman GTS 4.0 and 718 Boxster GTS 4.0, which both make 394 hp,". C/D panel (cd-2021-718-cayman-gts-4-0): "Power: 394 hp @ 7000 rpm". Still 394 hp for 2025 (kbb-2025-718-cayman).

weightLb.note: 2021 coupe with the 6-speed manual (standard transmission). Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision 9 October 2026: accepted at weight step 2; it is the measured test car). Quote: "Curb Weight: 3196 lb". The test car had comfort/interior options (18-way seats, GTS interior package, navigation, Bose audio; as tested $100,990 vs base $88,150). No Porsche US curb weight for this variant was found in the pages opened.
